chunks: As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from al-Hasan ibn ʿAli, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mughirah, from al-ʿAbbas ibn ʿAmir al-Qaṣabānī, from al-Muthannā al-Ḥannāṭ, from ʿAmr ibn Abī Naṣr, who said:
I said to Abī ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام: I had performed salat, then I remembered that I had not washed my private part after I had prayed. Should I repeat? He said: No.

So the correct approach regarding his saying عليه السلام, 'No,' is that we understand it to mean that repeating the wudu (ablution) is not obligatory upon him, because what is obligatory upon him is only to repeat washing the affected area. And there is nothing in the report stating that repeating the salat (prayer) is not obligatory upon him. What indicates this interpretation is what has already preceded from the reports, and that gives this even more clarification.

key_terms.أَغْسِلْ: to wash, here referring to cleansing after impurity

ai.seo_question: If someone remembers after salat (prayer) that he did not wash the private part, must he repeat the wudu (ablution) or the prayer?
ai.summary: This report discusses a legal ruling concerning ritual purity after salat (prayer) when one remembers not having washed the private part. The narration answers that wudu (ablution) itself does not need to be repeated, while the accompanying scholarly explanation clarifies that the report should not be taken to negate the need to repeat the salat (prayer).
